# nostr-shard-signer: full reference for coding agents

> Drop-in NIP-07 signer for web apps. One `<script>` tag plus `NostrBridge.init()` gives the page a standard `window.nostr`. Users sign in with their own NIP-07 extension or NIP-46 bunker, and, when a Web3Auth `clientId` is given, with Google/Apple/X (the key exists only inside a cross-origin iframe). Alpha software with no security audit; not for high-value keys.

Source: https://github.com/saintego/nostr-shard-signer
Types: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saintego/nostr-shard-signer/main/nostr-bridge.d.ts (plus the opt-in nostr-bridge-window.d.ts for `window.nostr`)

## 1. Prerequisites (the developer does these once, by hand)

Nostr-only sign-in (extension or NIP-46 bunker) needs nothing: call `NostrBridge.init()` without a `clientId`. The console then warns that Google/Apple/X sign-in is off.

For Google/Apple/X sign-in:

1. Create a Web3Auth project (Sapphire Mainnet) at https://web3auth.io and copy its client ID.
2. In the Web3Auth dashboard, under Project Settings → Domains → Allowlist URLs, add `https://saintego.github.io` (the signer iframe runs there) and the app's exact origin (e.g. `https://myapp.com`).
3. Open the portal at https://saintego.github.io/nostr-shard-signer/portal/, connect a Nostr key, and register the client ID together with the app's origin. The portal only accepts origins that are in the Web3Auth allowlist. To add origins later, use the portal's Update Domains tab.

The signer offers social login on an origin that is in the NIP-33 registry (step 3) or in the Web3Auth allowlist (step 2). If only one of them lists it, it still works and the console shows a `NOT_IN_REGISTRY` or `NOT_ALLOWLISTED` warning. The registry keeps working when Web3Auth's allowlist can't be read.

The portal refuses localhost, IP addresses and http origins. For local testing, add the localhost origin to the Web3Auth allowlist instead.

## 2. Complete example

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
  <head>
    <script src="https://saintego.github.io/nostr-shard-signer/nostr-bridge.js"></script>
  </head>
  <body>
    <p id="status">Loading…</p>
    <button id="login" hidden>Sign in</button>
    <button id="logout" hidden>Sign out</button>
    <button id="publish" disabled>Publish note</button>
    <script type="module">
      import { SimplePool } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/nostr-tools@2/lib/esm/index.js";
      const RELAYS = ["wss://relay.damus.io", "wss://nos.lol"];
      const statusEl = document.getElementById("status");
      const publishBtn = document.getElementById("publish");
      const loginBtn = document.getElementById("login");
      const logoutBtn = document.getElementById("logout");

      // Called with the current state once known (restored sessions included),
      // then on every sign-in / sign-out.
      NostrBridge.onAuthChange(({ loggedIn, pubkey }) => {
        statusEl.textContent = loggedIn ? "Signed in as " + pubkey : "Not signed in.";
        publishBtn.disabled = !loggedIn;
        loginBtn.hidden = loggedIn;
        logoutBtn.hidden = !loggedIn;
      });
      window.addEventListener("message", (e) => {
        if (e.origin === "" && e.data?.type === "SIGNER_ERROR")
          statusEl.textContent = e.data.message + " " + e.data.hint;
      });
      loginBtn.addEventListener("click", () => NostrBridge.login());
      logoutBtn.addEventListener("click", () => NostrBridge.logout());

      await NostrBridge.init({ clientId: "YOUR_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID" });

      publishBtn.addEventListener("click", async () => {
        const signed = await window.nostr.signEvent({
          kind: 1,
          created_at: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
          tags: [],
          content: "Hello Nostr!",
        });
        const pool = new SimplePool();
        await Promise.any(pool.publish(RELAYS, signed));
        pool.close(RELAYS);
      });
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```

### In a framework (React, Vue, Svelte…)

- Put the `<script src=…nostr-bridge.js>` tag in the HTML shell (`index.html`, `app.html`, or the root layout's head). Do not import it from JS.
- Call `NostrBridge.init()` client-side only (e.g. a top-level effect or `onMount`). It is idempotent: repeated calls (StrictMode, remounts) return the first call's promise, so no module-level guard is needed. With SSR, never call it on the server.
- Keep auth state in app state, updated from `NostrBridge.onAuthChange` (return its unsubscribe function from the effect's cleanup).
- TypeScript: copy `nostr-bridge.d.ts` into the project to type `NostrBridge`; its interfaces can be imported (`import type { NostrBridgeConfig, NostrBridgeAuthState } from "./nostr-bridge"`). It deliberately doesn't type `window.nostr`, so it coexists with other NIP-07 typings; add `nostr-bridge-window.d.ts` too if nothing else declares `window.nostr`.

React:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  NostrBridge.init({ clientId: "YOUR_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID" });
  return NostrBridge.onAuthChange(setAuth); // { loggedIn, pubkey }
}, []);
// <button onClick={() => NostrBridge.login()}>Sign in</button>
```

### Without an init call

The script tag can carry the config; the bridge then calls `init()` itself:

```html
<script src="https://saintego.github.io/nostr-shard-signer/nostr-bridge.js"
        data-client-id="YOUR_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID" data-layout="floating"></script>
```

Attributes map to the `init()` options: `data-client-id`, `data-bunker-origin`, `data-registrar-url`, `data-layout`, `data-button-size`, `data-mount-selector`, `data-force-iframe` (`"true"`/`"false"`). Any of them starts init, so `data-layout="floating"` alone gives Nostr-only sign-in. An explicit `init()` afterwards returns the same promise; `NostrBridge.ready` resolves when it is done.

## 3. API

### `NostrBridge.init(config): Promise<void>`

| Option          | Type                                | Default                                              | Notes |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `clientId`      | string                              | none                                                 | Web3Auth client ID; adds Google/Apple/X sign-in. Without it, only extension / bunker sign-in |
| `bunkerOrigin`  | string (absolute URL)               | `https://saintego.github.io/nostr-shard-signer`      | Only for a self-hosted signer |
| `registrarUrl`  | string                              | hosted registrar, when `bunkerOrigin` is the default | Only for a self-hosted signer |
| `forceIframe`   | boolean                             | `false`                                              | `true`: ignore an installed extension and don't offer bunkers; always use Web3Auth. Ignored without `clientId` |
| `layout`        | `"floating"` \| `"in-place"`        | `"floating"`                                         | Floating widget sits bottom-right |
| `buttonSize`    | `"standard"` \| `"large_social_grid"` | `"standard"`                                       | |
| `mountSelector` | string (CSS selector)               | none                                                 | Where the widget renders with `layout: "in-place"`; falls back to `<body>` |

Rejects if `bunkerOrigin` is not a valid URL (a corrected call may then retry). Later calls return the first call's promise and ignore their config. On load it:
1. Asks an installed NIP-07 extension for the pubkey (waits up to 5 s). If it answers, signing goes through it. If it doesn't (locked, or waiting for the user to approve), the sign-in chooser offers "Browser extension", and a late approval still signs the user in.
2. Without an extension, loads window.nostr.js so users can connect a NIP-46 bunker (nsec.app, Amber, nsecbunker). It can't load next to an extension, so extension users are not offered bunkers.
3. Replaces `window.nostr` with its own object, and injects the signer iframe (the Sign in button / avatar widget).
4. Restores a session from a previous visit if there is one.

### `NostrBridge.ready: Promise<void>`

Resolves once `init()` has completed, whoever called it (e.g. the `data-client-id` auto-init).

### `NostrBridge.onAuthChange(callback): () => void`

`callback({ loggedIn, pubkey })` runs on every sign-in / sign-out, only when the state changes. If the state is already known when you subscribe, it also runs right away, so a restored session is never missed. Returns an unsubscribe function. Can be called before `init()`.

The same data is dispatched as a `CustomEvent` on window: `window.addEventListener("nostr-bridge:auth", (e) => e.detail /* { loggedIn, pubkey } */)`.

### `NostrBridge.login(): Promise<void>`

Opens the sign-in modal, the same as the widget's "Sign in" button (it also offers the user's extension or NIP-46 bunker). Resolves once the modal was requested, or immediately if already logged in; the result arrives through `onAuthChange`. Rejects if `init()` was never called. Call it from a click handler.

### `NostrBridge.logout(): Promise<void>`

Signs the user out (Web3Auth session, or the extension/bunker connection as far as the bridge is concerned). Resolves once the logged-out state has been reported.

### `NostrBridge.getAuthState(): { loggedIn: boolean, pubkey: string | null }`

Synchronous current state.

### `NostrBridge.getSavedSession(): { pubkey, mode: "iframe" | "wnj" } | null`

Session cached in localStorage from a previous visit. Works before `init()`, e.g. to render the signed-in UI without a flash.

### `window.nostr` (standard NIP-07)

| Method | Returns | Notes |
| ------ | ------- | ----- |
| `getPublicKey()` | `Promise<string>` | 64-char hex pubkey |
| `signEvent({ kind, created_at, tags, content })` | `Promise<{ id, pubkey, sig, … }>` | `pubkey` is filled in by the signer |
| `nip04.encrypt(pubkeyHex, plaintext)` / `nip04.decrypt(pubkeyHex, ciphertext)` | `Promise<string>` | Legacy DMs |
| `nip44.encrypt(pubkeyHex, plaintext)` / `nip44.decrypt(pubkeyHex, ciphertext)` | `Promise<string>` | |

Behaviour:
- Calls made while the signer is still loading are queued. After that, calls made while logged out reject with "nostr-bridge: user is not logged in…".
- Don't rely on `window.nostr` calls to open a login prompt. The user signs in through the widget, or your button calling `NostrBridge.login()`.
- With Web3Auth login, kinds 1 (note) and 7 (reaction) are signed without asking. Other kinds, `nip04.encrypt` and both decrypts show a confirmation in the widget. Extensions and bunkers apply their own rules.
- With Web3Auth login, calls reject after 30 s without an answer from the signer, e.g. an unanswered confirmation.

## 4. Events

For auth changes, prefer `NostrBridge.onAuthChange` or the `nostr-bridge:auth` event (section 3). The bridge also dispatches `MessageEvent`s on `window`, kept for existing integrations and for `SIGNER_ERROR`. They have `event.origin === ""`. Ignore anything else, because real postMessage traffic always has a non-empty origin.

| `event.data` | When |
| ------------ | ---- |
| `{ type: "AUTH_STATE", loggedIn: true, pubkey }` | Sign-in, or session restored on load |
| `{ type: "AUTH_STATE", loggedIn: false, pubkey: null }` | Sign-out, or restored session expired |
| `{ type: "SIGNER_ERROR", code, message, hint }` | The signer iframe failed; see section 5 |

`AUTH_STATE` can fire more than once with the same value; make handlers idempotent. (`onAuthChange` and `nostr-bridge:auth` skip repeats.)

## 5. Errors and fixes

Signer errors are also logged with `console.error` in the host page as `nostr-bridge: signer error CODE: message`, followed by a hint. Non-fatal problems are logged with `console.warn` as `nostr-bridge: signer warning CODE: message`.

In the errors below that turn off Google/Apple/X sign-in, an extension or bunker still works through the Sign in button.

| Code / message | Cause | Fix |
| -------------- | ----- | --- |
| `CLIENT_ID_NOT_FOUND` | Web3Auth has no Sapphire Mainnet project with this clientId | Copy the right client ID, or leave `clientId` out for Nostr-only sign-in |
| `DOMAIN_NOT_REGISTERED` | The origin is neither in the NIP-33 registry nor in the Web3Auth allowlist | Register the exact origin (scheme + host + port) in the portal, or add it to the Web3Auth Allowlist URLs. The registry lookup is cached per browser tab, so test in a new tab |
| `NO_SIGN_IN_METHOD` | No `clientId`, and window.nostr.js failed to load | Check that cdn.jsdelivr.net is reachable, or pass a `clientId` |
| `NOT_IN_REGISTRY` (warning) | The origin is allowlisted in Web3Auth but not registered in the portal | Register it in the portal so sign-in keeps working when the allowlist can't be read |
| `NOT_ALLOWLISTED` (warning) | The origin is registered in the portal but not in the Web3Auth allowlist | Add it to the Web3Auth Allowlist URLs |
| `WEB3AUTH_INIT_FAILED` | Wrong clientId, or the signer origin is not allowlisted | Check the clientId; add `https://saintego.github.io` to the Web3Auth Allowlist URLs |
| `MISSING_ROOT_PUBKEY` | The signer can't reach the registrar | Omit `bunkerOrigin`/`registrarUrl` to use the defaults; if self-hosting, fix `registrarUrl` |
| `NOT_EMBEDDED` | `signer.html` was opened directly | Only load it through `nostr-bridge.js` |
| `LOGIN_FAILED` | The OAuth login failed (not cancelled) | Usually transient; the user can retry |
| "nostr-bridge: no clientId…" (warning) | `init()` without `clientId` | Expected for Nostr-only sign-in; pass a `clientId` to add Google/Apple/X |
| "nostr-bridge: bunkerOrigin must be an absolute URL…" | Bad `bunkerOrigin` | Omit it, or pass a full https URL |
| "nostr-bridge: user is not logged in…" | Call made before sign-in | Wait for `onAuthChange` with `loggedIn: true`, or call `NostrBridge.login()` from a button |
| "nostr-bridge: RPC timeout…" | No answer within 30 s | The user ignored the confirmation; retry |
| "nostr-bridge: already initialized …" (warning) | `init()` called again with a different clientId | The first config stays in effect; reload the page to switch |

## 6. Don'ts

- Don't install or import `nostr-bridge.js` from npm. It is only published as a script at the URL above.
- Don't assign `window.nostr` yourself after `init()`. The bridge keeps its own object there.
- Don't ask the user for their nsec or build a key-import UI. Users who have a key use an extension or a bunker through the widget.
- Don't expect npub values. Pubkeys are hex. Use nostr-tools `nip19.npubEncode` for display.
- Don't expect the bridge to publish events or talk to relays for the app.
- Don't hide or cover the widget container `#nostr-signer-container`. The sign-in modal and signing confirmations open in it, also after `NostrBridge.login()`.

## 7. Security model (short)

- With Web3Auth login, the private key is reconstructed only inside the cross-origin signer iframe. Parent-page JS, including XSS, cannot read it.
- Each (clientId, origin) pair must be in the NIP-33 registry on Nostr relays or in the clientId's Web3Auth allowlist (which only the project owner can edit) before Web3Auth sign-in works on a page. The registrar only registers origins that are in that allowlist.
- The signer is loaded from a CDN, so a compromise of the signer host could expose keys. Alpha, unaudited: not for high-value keys.

## 8. Self-hosting

Self-hosting means your own GitHub Pages signer, Cloudflare Worker registrar and root key. Pass `bunkerOrigin` and `registrarUrl`. See "Deployment" in https://github.com/saintego/nostr-shard-signer#readme.
